label: early original-phase steps (t=2-4) with favored current/previous/first tokens
explanation: Position-gated, token-modulated reset unit. Never fires at t=0,1 or on the delimiter; about 70% of activations (74% of mass) fall on original-phase steps t=2-5, peaking at t=3, with a secondary late-copy component (recall_idx>=5, ~25% of mass). Within the window, whether it fires is graded additive evidence from token identity: current input 1, l, m, x, z (input l and 1 strongest), previous input w, z, g, e, l, and first token d, c, f. Top activations are input l at t=3 in sequences starting with d (e.g. d w z [l]). When two of these cues coincide precision reaches 0.8, but a single cue is weak. The window alone has recall 0.70 but precision 0.13; the predicate trades recall for precision (dev F1 0.45, mass recall 0.67). It does not fire at t>=6 in the original phase or in early copy steps (recall_idx 0-4), and late-copy firing is not captured by the predicate.
